prediction: #787's third title answers differently from Kabuki: Tron's stalls ARE translation, and not because of a TLB flush. On disk (1-1791057797-lanelocal-2547673), the 120-frame hakuX-pages line holding each of Tron's eight stalls >= 400 ms after boot reads 15,785 to 48,572 blocks generated for seven of them and 2,186 for the eighth (the 1,375 ms stall at ~56 s of log) (Kabuki's: 20 to 861), and [rr425]'s sampled loop-gap time, which contains every tb_gen_code call, is 0.75 to 5.1 s over the stall windows (Kabuki's 698 ms stall: 64 ms). The 1,762 ms stall coincides with a jump-cache wipe that neither a TLB flush nor a TB invalidation made (jc - jct - jci = 1 at w=72), the trace a tb_flush() leaves: the whole code cache was thrown away and rebuilt (48,572 generated). The others carry 1.7k to 8.3k blocks discarded by code-page writes per line: code loaded into pages that held code. The 2,186-block stall is the one this prediction does not cover; it is reported, not forced into either reading. So: tb_gen_code time >= 400 ms in at least one stall, and the trigger is a code-cache flush or code loading, which [tcg787]'s tbf and disc name.

A stall with gus >= 400 ms, tbf = 0 and disc < 1,000 would be first-time translation of code never seen before, which no invalidation change can remove.
